title: Playing another boat; Lindbergh, the Depression and cheap food
summary: She subbed once on the Capitol, was in New York at Lindbergh's flight and in New Orleans for the Depression.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: The Depression years and the WPA band

blocks.x: Did you ever play on another boat beside the Madison?

Steamer Madison? I played one time on the Steamer Cap'n. I played more than playing piano on there, but he got sick one night and he had me to come to the place. He would just play for that. I wanted to ask you, where were you when Lindbergh crossed Atlanta? Where I was? I was in New York City then. You were in New York City then? I went there. I was in New York City. Did you see the Tick-a-Tape parade and all that? No I didn't get a chance to see it because I was in school. And where were you when the Depression hit? Right here in New Orleans. I'll never forget that. I see. It was tough. Times were hard. WPA was working then, men were working for the WPA then. Were you in the WPA? Oh and I guess you couldn't read much then. No I couldn't read much. Did you take the test? No I didn't take the test but I knew about it because I was playing with Sheik, Kit Sheik. He was playing with Bill Gordon then. Oh I see. That's when I met Kit Sheik. When the banks closed you mean? That's right. It was a mess I'm telling you. You always was a mess then. You could get, one thing about it though, food was cheaper then. You didn't make much money. But you could live, you know what I mean? Because you could take a dime and buy two things. You call it quarti. Quartii? Uh huh. Quartii beans, quartii rice? Yeah, that's half and half. You give them a dime for that. You ever hear of that? You have a meal. Oh yeah? I heard of that. Yeah sure, that's right. Quartii beans, quartii rice, and lanyard to make it nice. Yeah I used to buy all of that.
